reasoning:
Recent polling of Iowa’s 2026 U.S. Senate general election shows a very tight race with a slight Republican edge: the only fresh, clearly dated general-election poll in the last 45 days is the Emerson College/Nexstar survey from August 2–4, which has Ashley Hinson at 48% and Josh Turek at 45%, a **R+3** margin.[1][2][6][8] Coverage in the Des Moines Register, Iowa Capital Dispatch, and Newsweek in late July summarizes June polling (NYT/Siena Hinson +2, Fox News Turek +4) and forecaster ratings moving the race from “likely” to “leans Republican,” reinforcing that structurally Iowa still tilts right but the contest is competitive.[3][4][7][10] Taking the Emerson result as the only up-to-date quantified measure within the last 45 days, the best current estimate for the Iowa Senate race is **R+3**, while there is no recent, Iowa-specific 2026 presidential general-election polling in that window, so no current presidential margin can be reported.

For the Cook Partisan Voting Index, statewide Iowa has consistently been rated as a modestly Republican-leaning state (roughly **R+6**), and nothing in the recent PVI update chatter suggests a major shift from that range.[12][14][15] That structural R+6 environment contextualizes why major forecasters still list the 2026 Iowa Senate race as leaning Republican even as individual polls show a close contest.[3][4]

sources.name: Emerson College Polling / Nexstar Media
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar general-election survey of 712 likely Iowa voters finds Ashley Hinson 48% vs. Josh Turek 45%, an R+3 Senate margin.

sources.name: Newsmax
sources.details: Newsmax summary of the Emerson poll reports Hinson at 48% and Turek at 45% among likely voters in Iowa’s U.S. Senate race, describing the contest as competitive.

sources.name: Des Moines Register (NYT/Siena topline cited)
sources.details: Des Moines Register article cites a New York Times/Siena poll showing Hinson leading Turek 48% to 46% (R+2) and a Fox News poll from June 23-27 showing Turek leading 50% to 46% (D+4), and notes Cook and Sabato rate the race as lean Republican.

sources.name: Fox News (via Newsweek summary)
sources.details: Des Moines Register piece and Fox News coverage describe a Fox News poll of Iowa registered voters with Turek 50% vs. Hinson 46%, a D+4 margin in the Senate race.

sources.name: Iowa Capital Dispatch / Cook Political Report ratings
sources.details: Iowa Capital Dispatch notes Cook Political Report shifted Iowa’s Senate rating from ‘likely Republican’ to ‘leans Republican’ and summarizes early-July Fox News (Turek +4) and NYT/Siena (Hinson +2) polls as evidence of a tight race.

sources.name: CBS2 Iowa (local report on Emerson poll)
sources.details: CBS2 Iowa local report on the Emerson poll describes the Iowa U.S. Senate race as ‘still up for grabs,’ citing toplines of Hinson 47.5% vs. Turek 45% and emphasizing the close margin within the MOE.

sources.name: Bleeding Heartland (Emerson poll analysis)
sources.details: Bleeding Heartland’s analysis of the Emerson/Nexstar survey reports Hinson at 47.5% vs. Turek at 45.0% (R+2.5) and notes Turek leading among independents, underscoring the competitiveness of the Senate race.

sources.name: Newsbreak summary of Fox News and GSG polling
sources.details: Newsbreak summary references a Fox News survey of 1,003 Iowa registered voters showing Turek ahead of Hinson 50% to 46%, a D+4 margin, and mentions a prior internal Global Strategy Group poll with Turek +2.

sources.name: NBC News – Iowa Senate Primary Election 2026 Results
sources.details: NBC News reports the certified 2026 Iowa U.S. Senate primary results for Ashley Hinson and Josh Turek, providing context on the nominees but no general-election margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – 2026 Cook Partisan Voting Index (statewide context)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s updated PVI materials and related coverage indicate Iowa remains a modestly Republican-leaning state at approximately R+6 statewide, providing structural context rather than a specific 2026 race poll.
